newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe police rescue ministers from war veterans.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe police rescue ministers from war veterans.

text.p: Armed Zimbabwean police on Sunday rescued three cabinet ministers from angry war veterans demanding war victims' compensation, the official news agency ZIANA reported.

It said Defence Minister Moven Mahachi, Social Welfare Minister Florence Chitauro and Sports Minister Witness Mangwenda were escorted out through a back door after being besieged on a podium by hundreds of angry war veterans in Harare.
The heated four hour meeting was called to discuss government's suspension of the compensation fund.

The ministers ..."fled for their lives, leaving their official Mercedes Benz cars behind ... when the war veterans flooded the stage shouting (to Mahachi) 'you have said nothing, shut up, sit down'," the agency reported.
The veterans are demanding that President Robert Mugabe's government resume immediately payments of compensation which stopped in March to facilitate investigations into alleged fraud.

The fraud charges include allegations that some cabinet ministers had raided the fund in the past year by claiming to have suffered mental and physical disability of up to 90 percent as a result of the 1970s independence war.
Early this month, a number of angy male war veterans bared their scarred buttocks to Chitauro, one of three women cabinet ministers in Mugabe's team, to show her why they deserved compensation.

ZIANA and Zimbabwe state radio said the war veterans were in a "riotous mood" at several other meetings around the southern African state where Mugabe had deployed cabinet ministers to explain the government's position. Some veterans threatened to beat up the ministers, accusing them of being thieves and liars.

It said the ministers were generally abused, and at one meeting in south western Zimbabwe some former guerillas, who fought in Zimbabwe's independence war, told Home Interior Minister Dumiso Dabenga that Zimbabwe could face civil strife if the government continued to delay payments. They said their families were starving.
Many war veterans accused Mugabe's ministers of being thieves and demanded that Mugabe -- in power since 1980 -- address the war victims compensation problem himself.
There are an estimated 30,000 war veterans in Zimbabwe.
